title: When Data Inherits the Past
paragraphs: An algorithm is often imagined as a neutral referee, free of the prejudices that cloud human judgement. The difficulty is that most modern systems learn from historical data, and history is not neutral. If past decisions reflected unequal treatment, a model trained to reproduce those decisions can absorb the pattern and apply it with mechanical consistency, at a scale no individual official could match.

The problem is rarely announced by an explicitly prejudiced rule. More often it enters through a proxy, a variable that seems innocent but is correlated with something else. A widely cited study published in Science in 2019 examined an algorithm used in US health care to identify patients who needed extra care. Because it predicted future health spending rather than illness itself, and because less money had historically been spent on Black patients with the same level of need, it underestimated how sick those patients were. When the researchers reworked the target, the disparity fell substantially.

Measurement can expose such failures. A 2018 audit of commercial facial-analysis tools found that they classified the gender of darker-skinned women far less accurately than that of lighter-skinned men, and a 2019 evaluation by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology reported demographic differences in many face recognition algorithms, while noting that their size varied considerably from one system to another.

Correcting bias, however, is not simply a matter of better engineering. Researchers have shown that several intuitive definitions of fairness cannot, in general, be satisfied at the same time when groups differ in their underlying rates of the outcome being predicted. Choosing among them is therefore a question of values as well as of technique, and it is one that the people affected arguably have a right to help answer.

options.text: Algorithms may inherit bias, and fixing it involves values

options.text: Algorithms are more biased than human officials are

options.text: Bias in algorithms comes from openly prejudiced rules
options.explanation: Metne göre sorun nadiren açıkça önyargılı bir kuraldan gelir; çoğunlukla vekil değişkenlerden girer.

options.text: Better engineering will soon remove bias from software entirely
options.explanation: Yazar önyargıyı düzeltmenin yalnızca daha iyi mühendislik meselesi olmadığını söyler.
